tongariro-7.name: Tongariro Northern Circuit
tongariro-7.bio: A 35.5 km, three-to-four-day Great Walk around Tongariro and Ngauruhoe; one Whakapapa section is closed.
notes: DOC: 35.5 km one way (cut from 44.9 km; section closed after the 2025 Tongariro fire); placement said 43 km. Not operating as a Great Walk while Oturere Hut is replaced; 2026/27 starts at Mangatepopo Carpark and ends in Whakapapa Village.
Cost is the per-night hut fee, adult NZ 44 / international 66; about 3 nights, no entry fee. Coordinates moved from the loop centroid to Mangatepopo car park (OSM + Commons geotag).

tongariro-8.name: Turoa Ski Area
tongariro-8.bio: The ski field on Mount Ruapehu's southern slopes above Ohakune, with New Zealand's highest lifted point.
tongariro-8.hours: Winter ski season, from early July (closing date unverified)
notes: Adult day-pass 76-116 are spring-special prices on the operator page; standard price not shown. Closing date and daily lift hours not found. Coordinates at the base building (Wikipedia + OSM).

tongariro-9.name: Whakapapa Ski Area
tongariro-9.bio: The ski field on Ruapehu's northern slopes, where the Sky Waka gondola climbs to Knoll Ridge Chalet in summer.
tongariro-9.hours: Ski season 30 May – 25 Oct 2026; Sky Waka gondola 27 Oct 2026 – 30 Apr 2027
notes: Held for a photo. Placement bio said 'sightseeing chairlift': it is the Sky Waka gondola (12 min, 390 m climb). $59 is the winter scenic gondola adult ticket; summer price and ski day-pass not found. Coordinates at the Top o' The Bruce visitor centre.

tongariro-10.name: Waitonga Falls
tongariro-10.bio: A 4 km return DOC walk of about 1 hr 20 min to a 39 m waterfall, the park's highest, with views of Ruapehu.
notes: No Wikipedia article: no wiki field; needs a WIKI_IMAGE_OVERRIDES entry. Coordinates at the Ohakune Mountain Road car park (OSM). Open 24 hours is an assumption for an open-access track.

whanganui-7.name: Whanganui Regional Museum
whanganui-7.bio: A free museum in Pukenamu Queens Park with Māori taonga, moa bones and the Gottfried Lindauer Gallery.
notes: Closed Good Friday and Christmas Day only; closedDays omitted. Wikipedia article matches the name.

whanganui-8.name: Bason Botanic Gardens
whanganui-8.bio: A 25 ha botanic garden west of Whanganui with a conservatory, a large orchid collection and bush walks.
notes: Held for a photo. Free is inferred: no admission charge on the trust or council page. Coordinates at the visitor car park. Closing time varies through the year.

whanganui-9.name: Bushy Park
whanganui-9.bio: A predator-free forest sanctuary with over three hours of walking tracks and one of the largest northern rātā trees.
notes: Official name Tarapuruhi Bushy Park. Entry by koha (donation), recorded free: true; council page says free during daylight. Do not use bushypark.co.nz (spam site). Coordinates at the visitor car park.

whanganui-national-park-3.name: Atene Skyline Track
whanganui-national-park-3.bio: A 12.5 km one-way advanced track through forest above the lower Whanganui River, with views to Ruapehu and Taranaki.
notes: Placement visit time 4-6 hr corrected to DOC 6-8 hr. No Wikipedia article: needs a photo override. Trailhead point is an OSM track end (accuracy maybe 200-300 m). Halfway campsite has its own fee, not researched.

palmerston-north-4.name: Manawatū Gorge
palmerston-north-4.bio: An 11.2 km one-way DOC track through the gorge between the Ruahine and Tararua Ranges, with a shorter 4 km Tawa Loop.
palmerston-north-4.hours: Car park 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Oct–Apr), 6:00 AM – 7:00 PM (May–Sep)
notes: DOC calls it the Manawatu Gorge Track; placement said Te Āpiti track. Coordinates at Western Gateway car park (Ashhurst end). Visit 2-5 hr covers the Tawa Loop up to the one-way track (needs two cars).

palmerston-north-5.name: Feilding
palmerston-north-5.bio: A farming town north of Palmerston North with a Coach House Museum, a motor-racing circuit and a steam rail society.
notes: Town spot; no ticketUrl (no single steward). Whether a town qualifies is the owner's call. Coach House Museum was $12 per Wikivoyage (2020). Placement's clock tower is not source-checked, so left out.

ohakune-carrot.name: The World's Largest Carrot
ohakune-carrot.bio: A 7.5 m model carrot at Ohakune's Carrotland Adventure Park, in the same spot since 1984.
notes: ticketUrl omitted: Ruapehu District Council site is BLOCKED to scripts (HTTP 202) and unverified; orchestrator to check in a browser. No Wikipedia article: no wiki field; needs a photo override. Open 24 hours: roadside public park, no hours stated.

ohakune-old-coach-road.name: Ohakune Old Coach Road
ohakune-old-coach-road.bio: A restored 1906 coach road to walk or cycle, with cobbles, a curved tunnel and the 284 m Hapuawhenua Viaduct.
notes: Held for a photo. DOC full route 15 km one way (4.5 hr walk, 2 hr 20 min bike); visit 3-5 hr is out-and-back to the viaduct from Marshalls Road, an estimate. Coordinates at the Marshalls Road car park.

ohakune-dinosaur-house.name: Dinosaur House
ohakune-dinosaur-house.bio: A family museum in a 1922 building in Raetihi, with dinosaur skeletons, life-size reconstructions and fossils.
notes: Open Tue–Sun, closed Mondays. Adult (16+) $14. No Wikipedia article. Placement's 'more than 100' count was cut off in the source, so it is left out.

national-army-museum.name: National Army Museum
national-army-museum.bio: The national army museum on State Highway 1 at Waiouru, with self-guided visits and a one-hour guided tour.
notes: Open every day except Christmas Day. Self-guided adult $15, Express $17, Premium (1 hr tour) $19. Coordinates refined to the building.

taihape.name: Taihape
taihape.bio: A State Highway 1 town beside the Rangitikei River, billed as the Gumboot Capital of the World.
notes: Town spot; no ticketUrl. Whether a town qualifies is the owner's decision. Visit hours are an estimate.

taihape-gumboot.name: Taihape Gumboot
taihape-gumboot.bio: A giant corrugated-iron gumboot at Taihape, standing for the town as the Gumboot Capital of the World.
notes: Roadside sculpture, no steward site. No Wikipedia article: no wiki field; needs a photo override.

levin.name: Levin
levin.bio: The largest town in the Horowhenua District, on State Highway 1 beneath the Tararua Ranges near Lake Horowhenua.
notes: Town spot; no ticketUrl. Weakest keep per placement; Wikivoyage's see/do list is thin. Visit hours are an estimate.

marton.name: Marton
marton.bio: A Rangitikei district town, called Tūtaenui in Māori, with a population of about 5,500.
notes: Held for a photo. Thin keep: no visitor-oriented source for specific things to do was found, so the placement bio's walkway, reservoir and parks are not repeated. Town point from OSM.

foxton-1.name: Te Awahou Nieuwe Stroom
foxton-1.bio: A museum and cultural centre in Foxton telling Māori and Dutch heritage stories.
foxton-1.hours: Mon–Fri 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM, Sat–Sun 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM
notes: Spot of the proposed Foxton destination: stays out of apply-region until Foxton is approved. Entry by donation, free for Horowhenua residents, recorded free: true.

foxton-2.name: De Molen
foxton-2.bio: A working replica Dutch windmill with seven levels, a flour-milling demonstration and daily guided tours.
notes: Spot of the proposed Foxton destination. Self-guided $3 donation, guided $5; upper levels close 3:30 PM. Do NOT set wiki: 'De Molen' is a Dutch village. Needs a photo override. Placement's '17th-century' is unsourced and cut.

foxton-3.name: Foxton Beach
foxton-3.bio: A sandy beach settlement on the Foxton coast, formerly known as Manawatu Heads.
notes: Spot of the proposed Foxton destination. Placement's 'kitesurfing' and 'five minutes from Foxton' have no source and are cut. Coordinates approximate (no natural=beach way): run the water audit before shipping.

foxton-4.name: Waitārere Beach
foxton-4.bio: A beach village on the Horowhenua coast at the end of Waitarere Beach Road.
notes: Spot of the proposed Foxton destination; also held for a photo. Wikipedia title has no macron. Placement's 'surf beach, fishing' is unsourced and cut. Coordinates at the beach-end car park; run the water audit.

tongariro-1.bio: A 20.2 km one-way day walk across volcanic terrain, past the Red Crater and Emerald Lakes, taking 7 to 9 hours.
tongariro-1.hours: Daylight (Labour Weekend – 30 April; winter needs alpine skills)
tongariro-1.notes: DOC: 20.2 km (not 19.4), 7-8 hr Nov–Apr, 9 hr May–Oct. Pin moved ~3 km west to Mangatepopo car park (OSM + Commons geotag; DOC gives no coordinates). Bookings recommended and free.

tongariro-4.notes: No Wikipedia article for Tawhai Falls: remove wiki and rely on the photo override.

whanganui-3.notes: Operator: adult $2.50 each way, youth $1; weekdays 7:30–6, weekends and public holidays 9:30–5, closed Christmas Day. Replaces the old $6 / 5:30 PM.

whanganui-6.hours: Daytime cruises (sailing season about September – May)
whanganui-6.notes: Cost 45-55 and the season are from search snippets of the operator's pages (booking widget does not render for scripts): verify in a browser. Owner decision pending: reframe as the Taupo Quay wharf museum or remove (vehicle/operator).

whanganui-1.hours: Multi-day trips (Great Walks season 1 Oct – 30 Apr)
whanganui-1.notes: $35 is the DOC hut fee per person per night in the Great Walks season; canoe hire and guided trips cost much more and are operator-priced (not researched). Replaces the park-page link with the Whanganui Journey page.

whanganui-2.notes: Old link (park page) failed the title check. Visit Ruapehu lists the tour at adult $205; $190 is from a search snippet. Walk is 3 km return, 1 hr 30 min, after a jet boat to Mangapurua Landing.

palmerston-north-1.notes: The plain 'Te Manawa' title is a disambiguation page.

notes: Region manawatu-whanganui: new spots and fixes from research.json, placement.json and skeptic.json; Tawhai Falls, Durie Hill, Waimarie, Whanganui Journey, Bridge to Nowhere, Te Manawa, Tongariro Alpine Crossing are existing fixes.
Held for a photo (placement 'held: needs a photo'): Whakapapa Ski Area, Bason Botanic Gardens, Ohakune Old Coach Road, Marton, Waitārere Beach.
